caption:
"We don't get enough leads for that."

It's the first objection every small shop raises, and it gets the math backwards.

Fewer leads mean each one is worth more, and losing one costs more.

Most service businesses take hours to answer a new lead, not minutes. That gap barely hurts a high-volume shop. It guts a low-volume one, because there's no cushion of extra leads to cover the miss.

Automation doesn't scale up to matter. It runs the same on your third lead this month as it does on someone else's three-hundredth.

Test it on your own numbers before deciding it's overkill.
